LHX.sentence: L3Harris barely budged, but the thing to watch is its profit margins, which run noticeably thinner than the bigger defense contractors — whether they can fix that is what decides if today's low price is a bargain or a warning.

ASML.sentence: ASML ticked up again — as the only company on earth that makes the machines to print the most advanced chips, it stays expensive, and this week is nothing unusual.

LIN.sentence: Linde slipped a little, which is mildly interesting because this steady industrial-gas giant usually trades at a premium to its rival and right now it's priced about the same — a rare moment where the market isn't giving it its usual respect.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft dipped slightly, but it has quietly run far ahead of the other big tech names over the past month as its AI-cloud story keeps grinding along.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher eased back a touch, but biotech funding is thawing fast, and that money tends to show up in their lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is basically flat — this Canadian pipeline acts like a toll road on oil and gas and pays a generous dividend, and there's nothing dramatic happening this week.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow fell again and is now well off its high, which is unusual for a company whose AI-automation tools keep getting locked in by big corporations and government agencies on long contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore held flat while copper prices have been surging, which sets up a possible catch-up since this miner and trader should eventually follow the metal higher.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dipped slightly, but the real story is that the actual price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up — the headline number just looks weaker because of the mix of products sold, not because the business softened.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA drifted down a bit, but this Latin American Coke bottler stays cheap while the Mexican peso holds steady, so nothing's really wrong.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras rose this week as oil sits far above what it costs them to pump it, giving plenty of cushion behind that big dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk jumped this week, and even after the pop the shares are priced below what its fleet of container ships would cost to replace — a sign there's a floor under it.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped a little and is trading unusually close to Visa in value, but people keep tapping their cards everywhere, so the business itself is fine.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot company fell today and is now cheaper than it's been in years, even though hospitals keep doing more operations with its da Vinci machines — and each surgery means more supplies sold.
